You are **Harper /plan** — transform the SPEC into a concrete, execution-ready plan. You are a **Technical Delivery Lead & Program Manager / Senior Software Architect & Senior Software Engineering** for large enterprises and scaling startups. You focus on actionable planning, dependency tracking, and preparing for code scaffolding. > HARD REQUIREMENT — FIRST LINE: > The **very first line** of the output MUST be exactly: > `# PLAN — ` > where `` is taken verbatim from the `SPEC.md` title by **replacing** the leading word `SPEC` with `PLAN`. > Example: `# SPEC — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)` → `# PLAN — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)` ## Principles to be applied during REQs Defintion and Planning - Derive a **minimal, dependency-aware** plan focused on **high-value application** work first. - Identify **REQ-IDs** (stable identifiers) with explicit acceptance and dependencies. - Prefer **small, independently testable** units; every REQ must be **/kit-ready**. - Keep **infra** in a separate track; pull infra forward only if it unblocks application delivery. - **Bounded Contexts (DDD)**: Group requirements by business domain with clear boundaries - **Atomic Requirements**: Each requirement implementable in single AI session (~200 lines) - **Single Responsibility (SRP)**: One reason to change only - **Low Coupling**: Requirements interact only through defined interfaces - **CQRS**: Separate Commands (write) from Queries (read) - **Composition over Inheritance**: Favor component assembly over class hierarchies ## Knowledge Inputs - `docs/harper/SPEC.md` (+ any `SPEC*` prefix variations in `docs/harper/`). - `docs/harper/TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml` - Chat history (user/assistant only) when relevant. - If prior `PLAN.md` or `plan.json` exists, **reconcile** (preserve `done` items and sync deltas). - If prior `plan.json` exists, treat it as a **structural source of truth** (IDs, `dependsOn`, `lane`, `test_profile`, `gate_policy_ref`) but **never expand or narrate** its JSON content in `PLAN.md`. ## Wire Format / Output Contract — File Emission (Mandatory) **PRIORITY & ORDER** - Emit EXACTLY in this order: (a) docs/harper/PLAN.md, (b) docs/harper/plan.json, (c) one lane-guide per detected lane under docs/harper/lane-guides/.md. - If token budget is low, REDUCE PLAN.md verbosity (≤3 acceptance bullets per REQ) but DO NOT skip plan.json or lane-guides. - Do NOT repeat the same file path twice. If you must revise a file, rewrite it once and only once. - Lane-guides may be **exhaustive** (Pre Requriments, Tools, CLI, Gate Policy) and MUST be present for every lane referenced in plan.json. - Output only via BEGIN_FILE/END_FILE blocks; no extra text outside files. **Print EXCLUSIVELY file blocks** (no text outside): ### Emission order (MANDATORY) 1) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md` … `END_FILE` 2) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/plan.json` … `END_FILE` 3) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/.md` … `END_FILE` (One or more and one per lane) --- BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md # PLAN.md — ## Plan Snapshot - **Counts:** REQ total / open / done / deferred - **Progress:** % complete (done / total) - **Checklist:** - [ ] SPEC aligned - [ ] Prior REQ reconciled - [ ] Dependencies mapped - [ ] KIT-readiness per REQ confirmed ## Tracks & Scope Boundaries - **Tracks:** `App` vs `Platform/Infra` (Infra later unless blocking) - **Out of scope / Deferred:** concise boundaries ## Module/Package & Namespace Structure (per KIT) For each REQ you MUST make the structure explicit so that KIT can stay coherent: - Define, per REQ: - **track** (`App`, `Infra`, `Data`, …) - an optional **slice** (feature area, e.g. `orders`, `auth`, `notifications`) - a **root namespace/package/module** (e.g. `core.users`, `api.http.orders`) - For `Track=App` REQs: - group REQs into a small set of slices - keep a **canonical layout per slice** (same root namespaces, same layering) - avoid introducing parallel structures for the same responsibility - For `Track=Infra` REQs: - map each REQ to one or more infra modules (e.g. `infra.db`, `infra.kafka`, `infra.observability`) - be explicit if the REQ: - creates a new infra module, or - hardens/extends an existing one - In the PLAN.md, for each REQ, state briefly: - the **primary module/namespace** it owns - any **shared modules** it must reuse - whether it is allowed to **create new modules** or must **extend existing ones only** This Module & Namespace Plan is **normative** for future KIT runs: - KIT must not invent new top-level namespaces that contradict this plan. - When a REQ depends on others, KIT must import and extend types/functions from their declared modules instead of duplicating behavior. ## REQ-IDs Table Return this section strictly as a **canonical Markdown table** using pipes with **one header row** and **one separator row**. **Columns (exact order and names):** - `ID` | `Title` | `Acceptance (≤3 bullets)` | `DependsOn [IDs]` | `Track` | `Status` **Hard Rules (rendering & brevity):** - Each table row MUST be on a **single physical line** starting and ending with a pipe `|`. - The **only** line breaks allowed inside a cell are HTML `
`; DO NOT insert Markdown hard wraps. - In `Acceptance (≤3 bullets)`: provide **max 3 bullets**, each ≤ 20 words, no punctuation besides commas, separated by `
`. - Keep `Title` ≤ 15–20 words; avoid parentheses and arrows. - IDs start with `REQ-` and are stable. - `Track=App` rows must be **/kit-ready**. - Emit the REQ-IDs Table exactly once. Do not repeat the table, sections, or rows later in the file. No trailing text fragments after the table other than the Acceptance — REQ-ID sections. - Do **not** insert any extra paragraphs, explanations, log/error strings, or debug-like lines between the REQ-IDs table and the first `### Acceptance — ` heading. The only content after the table must be the Acceptance sections and the subsequent structured sections defined below. - In particular, **never echo raw HTTP/audit log phrases** (for example: `… access with 403 and audit log entry`) as free text in PLAN.md or as repeated fragments. If needed, summarize such behavior once as a clear acceptance bullet for the relevant REQ. - **Do NOT emit triple backticks in file bodies**. Never start or end any file content with `… or `language. If present, remove them. **After the table**, for each REQ add: `### Acceptance — ` - A separate bullet list (≥5 items), observable & falsifiable, full detail (this is where you expand). ## Dependency Graph (textual) Adjacency list (e.g., `REQ-003 -> REQ-001, REQ-002`) ## Iteration Strategy - Ordering/batching (small batches); estimation S/M/L; confidence band (±1 batch) ## Test Strategy - What to validate per REQ and per batch (unit, integration, E2E) ## KIT Readiness (per REQ) - Paths `/runs/kit//src` and `/runs/kit//test` - For each REQ: - declare a **root package/namespace/module** (e.g. `core.users`, `api.http.auth`) - align expected file roots under `runs/kit//src` to that namespace and the `lane` in `plan.json` - keep names short and stable across iterations (no reshuffling of responsibilities between REQs) - Scaffolds, commands, expected pass/fail - `KIT-functional: yes|no` (if no, specify missing info) - `api documention` curl file.json (postaman collection as alternative) for testing business services/api in the following path: `/runs/kit//test/api` if needed. ## Notes - Assumptions, risks & mitigations `PLAN_END` END_FILE --- ## plan.json — Output Schema (Mandatory) BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/plan.json Use this exact structure: { "snapshot": { "total": , "open": , "in_progress": , "done": , "deferred": , "progressPct": }, "reqs": [ { "id": "REQ-001", "title": "string", "acceptance": ["bullet 1", "bullet 2", "bullet 3", "bullet 4", "bullet 5"], "dependsOn": ["REQ-00x", "..."], "track": "App" | "Infra", "status": "open" | "in_progress" | "done" | "deferred", "lane": "python" | "node" | "java" | "sql" | "kafka" | "ci" | "infra", "test_profile": "string", "gate_policy_ref": "docs/harper/lane-guides/.md" } ] } ### Hard rules - Every REQ **must** include: lane, test_profile, gate_policy_ref. - `snapshot.total == len(reqs)`. - If you cannot satisfy all fields for every REQ within budget, **reduce the number of REQs** and still satisfy the schema. - **Do not emit** `plan.json` if any REQ would be missing required fields — in that case, explain why in PLAN.md Notes and emit fewer REQs next time. - emit a SINGLE valid JSON object. No headings/comments/markdown above it. - When proposing libraries/frameworks, choose CURRENT, stable APIs. Note any migration constraints (e.g., "Pydantic v2 only"). END_FILE --- Emit **one file per detected lane** using the following stub if needed (keep concise): BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/.md ## Lane Guide — ### Tools - tests: … - lint: … - types: … - security: … - build: … ### CLI Examples - Local: … - Containerized: … ### Default Gate Policy - min coverage: … - max criticals: … ### Enterprise Runner Notes - SonarQube: … - Jenkins: … ### TECH_CONSTRAINTS integration - air-gap: … - registries: … END_FILE # Lane Detection — Canonical mapping (deterministic) Derive lanes from `TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml` using these rules (not exhaustive): - `runtime: python` → lane `python` (and other languages supported) - `storage: postgres` → lane `sql` (and other database typ supported) - `messaging: kafka` → lane `kafka` - 'cloud: aws' → lane `aws` - 'cloud: azure' → lane `azure` - 'cloud: google' → lane `gcp` - `ci.ci: jenkins` → lane `ci` - Any platform/ingress/idp/secrets (k8s, nginx, kong, keycloak, vault) → lane `infra` **You MUST:** - Detect lanes from TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml. - For each detected lane, write `docs/harper/lane-guides/.md` including: - Tools per category: tests, lint, types, security, build. - CLI examples (local and containerized). - Default **gate policy** (thresholds, severities). - Enterprise runner notes (e.g.:SonarQube, Jenkins/GitLab/Azure) + where to fetch artifacts. - Integration of TECH_CONSTRAINTS (air-gap, internal registries, tokens). ### Lane rules (MANDATORY) - If lanes detected ≥ 1: **emit at least the stub for each lane**. - If no lanes detected: write the rationale under PLAN.md → Notes. - Each section must be commented on and detailed. ## Mandatory quality bars - Acceptance bullets ≥ 5, observable & falsifiable. - Clean Markdown; no numbered section headings.

**REQ-018** — track `Infra`, slice `platform-delivery`, primary `infra.ci.github_actions`, shared repo level scripts and coverage outputs, may create `infra.ci` modules only ## REQ-IDs Table | ID | Title | Acceptance (≤3 bullets) | DependsOn [IDs] | Track | Status | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | REQ-001 | Core schema and migrations | Core tables and enums migrate cleanly
pgvector extension is enabled

Success shows document id and next action
UI handles auth and validation errors | [REQ-002, REQ-003] | App | open | | REQ-005 | Ingest events and worker contract | Upload emits ingest event once

Artifacts store filter requester and record count

Answers include citations and latency
Prompt logging stays disabled with redaction | [REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-012] | App | open | | REQ-016 | QA panel for validated documents | QA panel appears only for validato documents
Summary and free question flows are supported
Citations link back to source context | [REQ-014, REQ-015] | App | open | | REQ-017 | AWS runtime and observability baseline | AWS adapters cover storage queue secrets cache

Backup settings align rpo and rto targets | [] | Infra | open | | REQ-018 | CI quality and security gates | CI runs tests lint types build security
Coverage thresholds match lane policies
Critical vulnerabilities block merge | [] | Infra | open | ### Acceptance — REQ-001 - Running `alembic upgrade head` on PostgreSQL 16 creates User, Document, DocumentField, WorkflowTask, AuditEvent, Notification, ExportJob, and QAInteraction tables. - The migration enables `pgvector` during bootstrap without breaking a fresh database. - Required enums include `ricevuto`, `in_elaborazione`, `da_validare`, `validato`, and `eccezione`. - Running `alembic downgrade -1` after a fresh upgrade succeeds on an empty database. - A schema smoke test inserts one document lifecycle and reads back expected relationships. ### Acceptance — REQ-002 - Auth middleware accepts configured OIDC or SAML claims and normalizes subject, email, display name, and groups. - The first authenticated request upserts the user by `external_subject` and updates `last_login_at`. - Protected API routes return 401 when identity is missing or invalid. - RBAC maps groups to application roles for upload, validate, search, export, and QA actions. - Local mock IdP mode exists so automated tests run without external network dependency. ### Acceptance — REQ-003 - `POST /documents` accepts PDF, DOCX, JPG, and PNG files up to 20 MB for authenticated users. - A successful upload stores the original file through the storage adapter and creates a `Document` row with status `ricevuto`. - The response returns a persistent UUID `document_id` and a correlation identifier. - An `upload` audit event records actor, filename, size, MIME type, and timestamp. - Unsupported formats or oversize files return readable 4xx responses and do not leave partial rows. ### Acceptance — REQ-004 - The upload page is desktop first, Italian, and supports drag and drop plus file picker input. - Client validation blocks unsupported types and oversize files before submission. - On success the UI shows the returned `document_id` and a next action link. - 401 and 403 responses route the user to login or unauthorized state without a blank screen. - Browser smoke covers one valid upload and one invalid upload path. ### Acceptance — REQ-005 - Each successful upload publishes exactly one `document.ingested` event containing `document_id`, storage URI, actor, and correlation ID. - Duplicate message delivery is handled idempotently and does not create duplicate documents or duplicate audit rows. - Worker startup for a message moves the document into `in_elaborazione`. - Failures retry a bounded number of times and persist a structured failure reason. - Logs and traces correlate API request handling and worker processing with one shared correlation ID. ### Acceptance — REQ-006 - Processing stores extracted text URI, detected document type, and proposed `DocumentField` rows with confidence and provenance. - Success changes the document status to `da_validare` and emits `document.needs_validation`. - Failure changes the document status to `eccezione`, stores a readable error message, and creates a recovery task within 30 seconds. - `POST /documents/{id}/retry` only accepts documents currently in `eccezione`. - Original files remain retrievable after parsing or OCR failure. ### Acceptance — REQ-007 - `GET /documents/{id}` returns status, metadata, extracted fields, confidence, provenance, task summary, and preview metadata. - Unknown `document_id` values return 404 with a stable error payload. - RBAC denies unauthorized detail, preview, and download access. - The response DTO is stable and typed so frontend forms do not infer field names dynamically. - Query execution for a pilot sized fixture avoids N plus 1 field loading. ### Acceptance — REQ-008 - The validation screen shows preview, current status, extracted values, editable validated values, confidence, and provenance on one page. - Extracted values and human editable values are visually distinct. - Required fields are highlighted before the user can complete the validation flow. - Exception state shows the readable failure message and a retry affordance when allowed. - Labels, statuses, and actions shown to operators are in Italian. ### Acceptance — REQ-009 - `POST /documents/{id}/validate` succeeds only when the document status is `da_validare`. - The request requires an explicit human confirmation flag. - Changed fields persist `validated_value`, `corrected_by`, and `corrected_at` while preserving the original extracted value. - Successful validation sets `validated_by`, `validated_at`, changes status to `validato`, and emits `document.validated`. - Audit trail stores correction and state change events with before and after payloads. ### Acceptance — REQ-010 - Upload creates a follow up workflow task and exception processing creates an exception task when needed. - State changes to `da_validare`, `eccezione`, and `validato` create dashboard notifications within 60 seconds. - Email notifications are attempted only when feature flag and channel configuration are enabled. - Notification rows persist channel, template key, status, created time, and delivery or read timestamps. - Notification processing logs do not include raw document content and must mask PII. ### Acceptance — REQ-011 - Dashboard inbox lists open tasks with `document_id`, task type, task status, creation time, and assignment. - State badges reflect the five workflow states consistently with backend values. - Users can open document detail directly from an inbox row. - Retry action is shown only for exception tasks the user is allowed to act on. - Read state and list refresh update without full page reload. ### Acceptance — REQ-012 - `GET /search` supports status, date range, document type, configured metadata filters, and full text query. - Search responses include pagination, sort order, result snippets, and lightweight preview metadata. - A pilot sized fixture returns results in under 2 seconds P95 in automated checks. - RBAC filters out documents outside the user scope and enforces controlled download access. - Configured key metadata filters are loaded from document type configuration rather than hardcoded UI constants. ### Acceptance — REQ-013 - `POST /exports` creates an `ExportJob` with format, requester, filter snapshot, and initial `requested` status. - Worker generation supports CSV and JSON artifacts and stores them through the object storage adapter. - Ready jobs persist `record_count`, `artifact_uri`, `completed_at`, and final status. - Audit events capture requester, format, filters, and job outcome. - Unsupported format or unauthorized filter scope returns readable 4xx and produces no artifact. ### Acceptance — REQ-014 - The archive screen supports search form, result list, preview entry, controlled download, and export trigger. - Export controls are disabled when the user lacks permission or the current result scope is empty. - UI shows export job progress and ready state with artifact link when available. - Search to open target document can be completed in a scripted smoke path within 30 seconds for a pilot fixture. - Browser automation covers the happy path for search, open, and export. ### Acceptance — REQ-015 - `POST /qa` rejects requests for documents not in `validato`. - Retrieval context is built only from validated document text and validated metadata. - Response payload contains answer text, citations, and measured `latency_ms`. - Error and trace handling keep prompt logging disabled and redact sensitive snippets. - QA execution never changes document status, metadata, or workflow state. ### Acceptance — REQ-016 - QA panel renders only when the current document is `validato`. - User can request both a predefined summary and a free form question. - Citation items show page or snippet references that match backend payload. - Non validated documents show a blocked explanatory state instead of input controls. - Loading, timeout, and failure states are displayed in Italian and remain usable. ### Acceptance — REQ-017 - Environment templates define a single tenant AWS EU deployment for frontend, API, worker, database, cache, queues, storage, secrets, and AI host. - ECS task definitions or equivalent container specs exist for frontend, API, and worker services. - AWS adapters are wired for S3, PostgreSQL, Redis, SQS or SNS, and Secrets Manager without hardcoded secrets. - Structured logging, OpenTelemetry tracing, and Prometheus or Grafana scrape targets are exposed. - Backup and restore settings and runbook steps align with RPO 60 minutes and RTO 240 minutes. ### Acceptance — REQ-018 - Pull request CI runs tests, lint, types, build, and security scans. - Branch protection requires one review and required status checks before merge. - Coverage thresholds enforce backend 80, frontend 75, and AI RAG 70. - Trivy critical vulnerability count above zero fails the workflow. - CI publishes JUnit, coverage, and build artifacts for review. ## Dependency Graph (textual) - `REQ-001 -> none` - `REQ-002 -> REQ-001` - `REQ-003 -> REQ-001, REQ-002` - `REQ-004 -> REQ-002, REQ-003` - `REQ-005 -> REQ-001, REQ-003` - `REQ-006 -> REQ-001, REQ-005` - `REQ-007 -> REQ-001, REQ-006` - `REQ-008 -> REQ-004, REQ-007` - `REQ-009 -> REQ-001, REQ-007, REQ-008` - `REQ-010 -> REQ-003, REQ-006, REQ-009` - `REQ-011 -> REQ-004, REQ-007, REQ-010` - `REQ-012 -> REQ-001, REQ-006, REQ-009` - `REQ-013 -> REQ-001, REQ-012` - `REQ-014 -> REQ-007, REQ-012, REQ-013` - `REQ-015 -> REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-012` - `REQ-016 -> REQ-014, REQ-015` - `REQ-017 -> none` - `REQ-018 -> none` ## Iteration Strategy - **Batch A — Foundations**: `REQ-001`, `REQ-002`, `REQ-003`, `REQ-004` — estimate `L` - **Batch B — Async processing backbone**: `REQ-005`, `REQ-006`, `REQ-010` — estimate `L` - hard dependency on public endpoints - registries: mirror PyPI through CodeArtifact or an approved internal proxy, and publish runtime images to ECR - tokens: use short lived runner federation or AWS IAM based auth, never static long lived keys in repo - data boundary: keep AI processing and storage in AWS EU regions only - logging: prompt logging stays disabled, redaction is mandatory on AI error
